Daily Brief

Sunday's news is dominated by escalating military actions across multiple theaters. Ukraine launched what Moscow's mayor called an 'unprecedented' drone attack on the Russian capital, with 450 drones intercepted and at least two civilians killed, while an oil refinery was damaged [BBC, ABC Australia, Le Monde]. The attack coincides with the final day of Russia's first wartime parliamentary election. In the Middle East, Houthi militants struck the Saudi capital Riyadh with ballistic missiles for the first time since escalating hostilities in July, prompting US travel warnings [BBC, France 24, Financial Times, Al Jazeera]. Diplomatically, the US and Denmark announced a security agreement over Greenland, resolving months of tension sparked by President Trump's annexation threats, with NATO welcoming the deal [BBC, The Economist, France 24]. In Germany, state elections in Berlin and Mecklenburg-Vorpommern could deliver another blow to Chancellor Merz's CDU following the far-right AfD's recent gains [BBC, Financial Times, Le Monde]. Meanwhile, French President Macron warned of intensifying Russian hybrid attacks against Europe and ordered enhanced protection of critical infrastructure [BBC].

Ukraine Launches 'Unprecedented' Drone Attack on Moscow, Killing Two

  • Moscow Mayor Sobyanin reported 450 drones were shot down en route to the capital in what he called an 'unprecedented attack'; Russia's Defense Ministry claimed 1,100 Ukrainian drones were intercepted nationwide

03 Geopolitics

US and Denmark Reach Greenland Security Deal After Months of Trump Threats

  • The US and Denmark announced a security agreement granting the US 'permanent control over security' in Greenland, according to President Trump, though no official text has been released
  • The deal reportedly prohibits any US adversary from maintaining military presence or making sensitive investments in Greenland without US approval
  • NATO welcomed the agreement as helping 'advance security, stability and cooperation' in the Arctic region
  • The deal resolves diplomatic tensions sparked by Trump's repeated threats to 'take' Greenland by force, citing its strategic location and mineral wealth

German State Elections Threaten Fresh Blow to Chancellor Merz

  • Voters in Berlin and Mecklenburg-Vorpommern are casting ballots in state elections where polls suggest Chancellor Merz's CDU faces potential defeats
  • In Mecklenburg-Vorpommern, the CDU is polling near the 5% threshold required to enter the state parliament, risking their worst-ever state election result
